content.text:
`--legacy-imports` makes the build also write `pkg/_legacy.py` into the bundle (`scripts/build.py:18-20`). That file re-exports `group_totals` as `sum_by` and `parse_amount` as `to_decimal`, which are their pre-1.0 names. Without the flag, anyone still importing the old names from the bundle would break.

So it isn't dead code. It's a backward-compatibility shim for old callers.

The runbook doesn't say why the release passes the flag, so I can't tell whether it's still needed. I don't know whether anyone still uses the old names or whether the shim was meant to be temporary. Dropping the flag would remove those names from the published bundle without warning. Nothing in the repo shows who depends on them, so that decision is yours. If you want it gone, I'd drop it from step 4 and note the removal in the changelog.

I haven't changed anything. Step 4 still needs the build to be approved, as before.
